A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with GSA renamed NCRL in v3. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–K are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments across 72 tasks, continual adaptation, and component ablations, including Figures 3–11 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and adaptation results and adds original aligned-baseline comparisons, retrieval evaluations, sensitivity tests, and extended-training experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The RSSM architecture, retrieval, rehearsal, and policy-switching procedure remain matched. However, v3 replaces the single-KL loss expression with separately weighted, stop-gradient dynamics and representation losses, and changes the actor objective from expected critic value to the lambda-return. The PDFs do not establish whether these reflect implemented training changes or corrections and expanded documentation of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DMControl and Meta-World coverage: 72 tasks, six embodiments, and 60k offline trajectories. The additional studies reuse existing tasks and data while varying retrieval composition, configurations, or training budgets. The Ant/Quadruped wording change accompanies the same continual-adaptation task sequence.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated iVideoGPT-align comparison, including Assembly, which was absent from v2's iVideoGPT comparison panels (Appendix A.2, Figure 10). The original comparator sets remain. UDS-RLPD denotes the UDS-plus-RLPD combination already used in v2; DreamerV3-Align chiefly introduces a model-size control.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds substantial evaluation controls: iVideoGPT fine-tuning on the authors' dataset with behavior-cloning initialization, no reward shaping or demonstration pre-filling, and a 200k-step comparison; a DreamerV3 model-size match; retrieval precision at 250/500 trajectories; and guidance-schedule and retrieval-contamination sweeps. Selected difficult tasks also receive longer training budgets. The original benchmark budgets and Appendix J hyperparameters remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, OTS, and world-model fine-tuning ablations, v3 adds retrieval accuracy analysis (Table 2), guidance-schedule sensitivity (Figure 12), task-irrelevant retrieval injection (Figure 14), baseline-capacity sensitivity (Figure 15), and extended-budget analysis of difficult tasks (Figure 16). These investigate previously untested questions about retrieval reliability, robustness, and performance bottlenecks.

E5.justification: v2 states three seeds per task. v3 Appendix I and Figures 17–19 report five seeds for NCRL and three for the baselines, although the main text and compute estimate retain three-seed statements. Mean/confidence-interval reporting already existed; v3 additionally displays uncertainty bands for the full per-task benchmark curves.

E6.justification: Many benchmark estimates change alongside the revised seed reporting: Assembly success changes from 0.20 to 0.44, Soccer from 0.67 to 0.16, and mean DMControl return from 631.10 to 617.73. DreamerV3's reported Meta-World mean at 1M steps changes from 0.900 to 0.656 despite unchanged task entries. v3 also adds extensive control and robustness results, including failure with 100% task-irrelevant retrieval in Figure 14. These are updated estimates and additional settings, not established method-level performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 replaces v2's alpha-coupling argument and uniformly positive guide-advantage assumption with an explicit mixed policy and an expected-advantage bound containing a distribution-shift penalty, invoking Kakade and Langford. The forgetting proposition becomes an explanation. This substantially revises the formal support, although v3's prose condition for positive improvement does not match the sign required by Equation 11.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the precise 102.8% relative-improvement headline with nearly twice the aggregate score, and the introduction removes the claim of evaluating 12 times more tasks than previous baselines. The four principal contributions, distribution-shift motivation, and sample-efficiency and adaptation claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations that online collection and imagined rollouts mitigate occasional retrieval errors, and attributes difficult Meta-World tasks to long horizons, small objects, and strict success criteria. It also introduces broad robustness interpretations, although Figures 12 and 14 expose failures without guidance or with entirely irrelevant retrieval. Appendix D's substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a project code-and-dataset access link, specifies the Dreamer policy-update version followed, discloses the smaller original DreamerV3 baseline configuration, and corrects the behavior-cloning code's return typo. Hardware, runtime estimates, and hyperparameter tables remain largely unchanged. Conversely, the explicit Meta-World Gaussian-noise grid in v2 is shortened to a maximum noise level of 2.0.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Kakade and Langford, Mereu et al., and the DMControl and Meta-World benchmark papers, while removing the TRPO reference used by the earlier proof. Table 1 changes RLPD's training-stability classification from negative to positive. The broader research positioning remains; much of the expanded appendix review preserves material from v2's main related-work section.

P1.justification: v3 consistently renames GSA to NCRL and generalist world models to task-agnostic world models, edits introductory and methodological explanations, and condenses the main related-work section while retaining detail in Appendix C. It also moves the ethics statement and adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. The overall methods–experiments–conclusion organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds a retrieval-precision table, five comparison/analysis figures, and three extensive per-task learning-curve figures. Existing plots receive revised sizing, labels, legends, and axis ticks, and the document adopts ICLR formatting. Earlier appendix figures are retained under renumbering: v2 Figures 10–12 correspond to v3 Figures 11, 13, and 20.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical credibility by adding aligned iVideoGPT and matched-capacity DreamerV3 comparisons, addressing important comparison gaps in v2. Retrieval diagnostics, stress tests, and full per-task curves with five NCRL seeds reported make the central mechanisms and performance limits more assessable. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: ambiguous seed reporting, robustness prose that understates Figure 14's failure boundary, and the inconsistent positivity condition in Appendix B.2. The improvement rests on stronger validation and transparency, rather than higher reported scores.
